property_statement: Committed-entry agreement / Log Matching: once index i is committed in a term t on the leader side, every node that later advances its commit index past i must contain (and apply) the same entry identity at index i as the rest of the committed quorum. Equivalently, on the follower append path, if an incoming MsgApp carries an entry at index j while the follower already holds a conflicting (different-term) entry at j, the follower must truncate/replace from j (completing LogReplaceOrDelete) before acknowledging any index >= j, and must never later commit or apply the stale conflicting entry at j.
summary: In go.etcd.io/raft/v3 `raftLog.maybeAppend`, a skip guard drops the first (empty/no-op) entry of a multi-entry MsgApp from conflict detection whenever its index equals the follower's last index. The guard is only behaviourally relevant when the follower's tail entry at that index has a conflicting term: instead of truncating and overwriting it with the leader's empty entry (the correct Raft conflict-resolution), the follower retains the stale entry, appends the remaining entries, and still acks the full index range. The leader's commit propagation then marks the stale divergent entry locally committed and applied on that follower, diverging from the committed entry applied by the rest of the quorum. Reachability requires a cluster where one isolated voter holds a single uncommitted extra entry at the exact index where a newly elected, shorter-log leader writes its no-op entry (e.g. >=5 voters), and where the leader's earlier single-entry (no-op only) append never reaches that follower (drop/reorder allowed by the fault model). This is a candidate mechanism, not a confirmed defect; execution evidence would still be needed to prove the state is schedulable.

source_evidence.claim: maybeAppend drops the message's first entry from conflict detection when check[0].Index == follower lastIndex, check[0].Data is empty and a data entry follows, then appends a.entries[ci-offset:] where ci comes from the truncated check. When the follower's tail entry at that index conflicts (different term), findConflict returns the conflict index i only if check[0] is scanned; with the skip, ci is >= i+1 so the stale tail entry at i is never truncated/replaced while lastnewi = prev.index + len(entries) is acknowledged anyway.

handleAppendEntries accepts the leader MsgApp exclusively through raftLog.maybeAppend(a, m.Commit) and, on ok, replies MsgAppResp{Index: mlastIndex} with no further reconciliation of any divergent prefix below the acked index.

maybeSendAppend builds MsgApp from pr.Next with LogTerm/term of prevIndex and attaches the leader's current committed index (Commit: r.raftLog.committed). A newly elected leader thus sends its no-op plus all later proposals in one message, so the two-plus-entry pattern is the first append a reconnecting follower can see.
reset() on becoming candidate/leader sets every remote progress to Match=0, Next=leader.lastIndex+1, so appends to an uncontacted follower start exactly at the new leader's no-op index.
becomeLeader appends an empty (Data:nil) no-op entry as the first entry of the term, producing exactly the empty first entry that triggers the maybeAppend skip in subsequent two-plus-entry appends.

MaybeUpdate blindly raises pr.Match to whatever index the follower acknowledged, without verifying that the follower's log actually matches the leader's through that index; the inflated ack from the divergent follower therefore counts toward the leader's commit tally.

stepLeader on a non-rejected MsgAppResp calls MaybeUpdate(m.Index) and then r.maybeCommit(), so an ack of the follower's lastnewi (covering the retained conflicting entry) can advance the commit index; after commit, further MsgApp/heartbeats carry the new Commit to the divergent follower.

commitTo only requires tocommit <= lastIndex and monotonically advances committed; it does not verify entry identities, so a follower whose commit pointer moves past a stale conflicting local entry will treat that entry as committed.

nextCommittedEnts/maxAppliableIndex deliver for application every local entry in (applying, committed], meaning the divergent stale entry at the conflicting index is returned to the application on that follower.

mechanism.violated_obligation: When a follower accepts a MsgApp whose entries begin at index i while the follower already holds a conflicting entry at i, it must truncate from i and replace with the leader's entries before acknowledging any index >= i (follower-side Log Matching obligation), so that commit advancement can never mark a divergent entry at a committed index as committed/applied.
mechanism.decisive_relation: The skip guard `len(check) > 1 && check[0].Index == l.lastIndex() && len(check[0].Data) == 0 && len(check[1].Data) > 0 { check = check[1:] }` removes the only entry whose conflict would be detected at the follower's tail; findConflict then returns ci = i+1 (the first truly new entry) instead of i, so `l.append(a.entries[ci-offset:]...)` appends only entries after the no-op, and the stale conflicting follower tail at i survives while `lastnewi = a.prev.index + uint64(len(a.entries))` is returned as the acknowledged/committed boundary.

causal_chain: A fixed-membership cluster (>=5 voters) has an isolated voter C whose log tail holds a single uncommitted data entry (i, term t1), while a majority (whose logs end at i-1) elects leader L at term t2 > t1; L's no-op entry therefore occupies exactly index i.

L's first append that reaches C (all earlier single-entry no-op-only appends to C having been dropped/reordered) carries [empty@i(t2), data@i+1(t2)] with prev=i-1; the maybeAppend skip fires because check[0].Index == C.lastIndex()==i, so C retains (i, t1, data), appends only from i+1, and acks lastnewi=i+1; L raises C.Match to i+1 and may commit i+1 on a majority.

C's commit pointer advances to >= i+1 (via the Commit field of L's append), and nextCommittedEnts/apply delivers C's stale divergent entry (i, t1, data) as committed/applied, while L and the other majority nodes committed/applied (i, t2, empty) - i.e. two distinct entry identities committed/applied at the same index, violating committed-entry agreement / state-machine safety.

test_sketch.precondition: P: 5-node fixed voter cluster {1,2,3,4,5}, every log identical through committed index 10 (term 1). Node 1 is term-1 leader; node 3 is the to-be-divergent follower. Leader 1 has crashed after replicating exactly one extra entry (11, t1, data 'X') to node 3 only (dropped to 2,4,5), leaving node 3's last index = 11 while nodes 2,4,5 end at 10.
actions: A1: Nodes 2,4,5 elect node 2 as leader in term 2 (majority of 5) while node 1 stays down and node 3 rejects but cannot win; node 2 appends no-op (11, t2). Drop node2->node3 MsgApp that contains only the no-op entry so node 3 keeps (11, t1, 'X').
A2: Node 2 proposes entry 'Y' at index 12 and replicates it to nodes 4 and 5 only; node 2 commits index 12 on quorum {2,4,5}.
A3: Trigger node 2's heartbeat/append retry toward node 3 and deliver to node 3 the first append it ever processes from node 2: MsgApp(prev=10, entries=[no-op(11,t2), 'Y'(12,t2)], Commit=12).
A4: Let node 3 respond MsgAppResp(Index=12) and process application of committed entries 11..12.
test_sketch.violation: V: node 3 never overwrites entry 11; after A3/A4, node 3 has committed and applied entry (11, t1, 'X') at index 11 while nodes 2,4,5 have committed and applied (11, t2, empty), so two distinct entry identities are committed/applied at the same index and node 3's applied state diverges.
test_sketch.oracle: O: Externally observable as: (a) node 3's acknowledged MsgAppResp index equals 12 while node 3's log entry at index 11 still has term 1/payload 'X' (LogContains(3,11,(t1,'X')) true and no LogReplaceOrDelete(3,11,...) completes); and (b) comparing the applied entry at index 11 across nodes yields differing (index, term, payload) after the commit of 12.

uncertainties: Reachability of the divergent state is not proven: it requires a >=5-voter configuration where an uncommitted entry exists on exactly one isolated voter at precisely the index where the next elected (shorter-log) leader writes its no-op, and requires that no single-entry (no-op-only) MsgApp is ever processed by the divergent follower before the multi-entry one (message drop/reorder is within the fault model).

If the divergent follower holds two or more extra entries beyond the leader's last index, the skip does not fire (check[0].Index != lastIndex) and normal conflict truncation occurs; the harmful window is exactly one extra entry.

Whether some other path (snapshot delivery, later higher-term overwrite, or entry compaction) would repair the divergence before or at the point of application is not established by the inspected source.
Async-storage-writes interactions (unstable offsetInProgress, stableTo term-mismatch checks) may alter whether the stale entry is retained/persisted; not evaluated in this run.
No execution harness was available to confirm the message scheduling; the mechanism and its decisive ordering are supported statically by the inspected code.
